analysis.summary: This PR, titled 'Feature/techus update node pnpm', contains multiple high-severity functional changes and severe PR scope violations beyond a Node.js and pnpm update. The most critical issues involve a complete map provider switch, extensive GraphQL schema modifications, and inconsistent outlet selection logic.

bugs.title: PR Scope Violation: Complete Map Provider Switch (Here Maps to AWS Location Service/MapLibre GL JS)
bugs.lineHint: Lines 123-144 (dependencies block) and multiple src/feature-app/components/AwsMap and src/feature-app/components/HereMaps files
bugs.description: The PR completely replaces the Here Maps implementation with AWS Location Service using MapLibre GL JS. This involves adding new map libraries (maplibre-gl, maplibre-gl-js-amplify), removing old ones (@here/maps-api-for-javascript), and introducing several new UI components and utility files for the AWS map, while deleting all corresponding Here Maps files.
bugs.risk: This is a high-severity functional change, as it replaces a core UI component with an entirely different technology stack. It is a severe PR scope violation for a 'tech update node pnpm' PR. This change implies a new feature or major refactoring is being deployed without appropriate review under the stated PR intent, risking significant regressions, performance issues, cost implications, and requiring extensive, dedicated testing not typically associated with a tooling update.

bugs.title: PR Scope Violation: Extensive GraphQL Schema Modifications
bugs.lineHint: Multiple lines throughout the file, adding and removing types and fields
bugs.description: The PR includes a massive update to the GraphQL schema types. Numerous new types (e.g., LiuxiModel, MiniCartFeatureAppContentExtendedWarrantyModel, PaymentCalculatorContentExtendsModel, ProductCatalogueIncompatibleExtendedWarrentyModalModel) are introduced, and existing types have new fields (e.g., headlineTag on CampaignBannerModel).
bugs.risk: This is a high-severity functional change and a severe PR scope violation. Changes to the GraphQL schema fundamentally alter the application's data contracts. If the backend GraphQL API has not been updated in sync with these new types, or if other parts of the frontend application rely on the old schema and are not updated, this will lead to runtime errors (e.g., 'Cannot query field X on type Y'), data fetching failures, and incorrect application behavior. Such extensive changes require a dedicated feature PR and thorough integration testing.

bugs.title: Inconsistent Outlet Selection and URL Parameter Handling
bugs.description: The PR introduces inconsistent behavior for managing the 'bpid' URL parameter when an outlet is selected. The logic for adding/removing the 'bpid' search parameter and updating browser history (`window.history.pushState`) has been removed from `Outlet.tsx` (for list item selection) but is explicitly re-added in `OutletLocator.tsx` within the `handleMarkerClick` function (for map marker selection). Additionally, `unSetBpidVariant` is used to conditionally prevent selected outlet data from being passed for certain variants.
bugs.risk: This is a high-severity functional bug that will cause confusing user experience and break application state management. Users interacting with the outlet list will not see URL changes, while those interacting with the map will. This inconsistency affects deep-linking, browser history, and how external systems or other feature apps might integrate with the `bpid` parameter. It's a critical functional regression and a PR scope violation.

notBugs.reason: Changes in `.buildkite/pipeline.yaml`, `README.md`, `.npmrc`, `package.json` (Node.js version, pnpm setup, TS updates), `tsconfig.json`, `types/scss.d.ts`, and `webpack.config.js` are directly related to the stated PR intent of updating Node.js and migrating to pnpm. These are expected and necessary updates for a tech stack migration.

Changes in `src/feature-app/components/LocationSearch/location-search.module.scss` and `src/feature-app/components/app.module.scss` are styling adjustments that, while functional changes, do not represent high-severity bugs or a significant scope deviation on their own, especially in the context of a new map component introduction.
